name: kisetsu-sango-kaku
title: Sango-kaku
text: Coral-bark maple. The winter twigs are the point: the leaves go butter-yellow and fall, and the bare branch turns coral.

name: kisetsu-bloodgood
title: Bloodgood
text: The one everyone plants. Deep burgundy all summer, then scarlet; upright and reliable, which is why it is everywhere.

name: kisetsu-osakazuki
title: Osakazuki
text: Green until it is not. Osakazuki holds plain green through summer and then turns the most violent crimson of any palmatum.

name: kisetsu-seiryu
title: Seiryu
text: The only upright laceleaf. Dissected foliage that stays green through the heat and finishes gold with a red edge.

name: kisetsu-shishigashira
title: Shishigashira
text: Lion's mane. Crinkled leaves crowded on short internodes, so the whole tree reads as texture before it reads as colour.

name: kisetsu-katsura
title: Katsura
text: Spring, not autumn, is its season: new leaves open apricot-orange, fade to green, and come back gold in October.

name: kisetsu-beni-kawa
title: Beni-kawa
text: Red-bark, the redder sibling of Sango-kaku. Same trick, harder colour, and the bark brightens as the temperature drops.

name: kisetsu-aconitifolium
title: Aconitifolium
text: Fernleaf full-moon maple, an Acer japonicum rather than a palmatum. Deeply cut fans that turn every shade of red at once.

name: kisetsu-orange-dream
title: Orange Dream
text: Opens orange-yellow in spring with a red margin, greens in summer, golds in autumn. Three trees in one year.

name: kisetsu-crimson-queen
title: Crimson Queen
text: Weeping dissectum. Holds its dark red through summer heat better than most laceleaf forms, which is the whole selling point.

name: kisetsu-viridis
title: Viridis
text: The green weeping laceleaf. A mound of dissected foliage that goes gold and orange, the counterweight to Crimson Queen.

name: kisetsu-higasayama
title: Higasayama
text: Variegated: cream margins on green, flushed pink as the leaf opens. Closest thing in the genus to a printed pattern.

name: kisetsu-somei-yoshino
title: Somei-yoshino
text: The clone. Nearly every famous avenue in Japan is one genetically identical tree, which is why a city blooms on the same day.

name: kisetsu-yamazakura
title: Yamazakura
text: The wild hill cherry: flowers and copper-red young leaves open together, so the tree is never pure white the way Somei-yoshino is.

name: kisetsu-shidarezakura
title: Shidarezakura
text: Weeping. The branches carry the flowers down rather than up, and the oldest specimens are propped on timber frames.

name: kisetsu-kanzan
title: Kanzan
text: Double, deep pink, thirty petals or more per flower. Blooms late, after the single whites have gone over.

name: kisetsu-ukon
title: Ukon
text: The yellow-green cherry. Pale chartreuse petals that pink at the base as they age, which reads as a printing error and is not.

name: kisetsu-jugatsuzakura
title: Jugatsuzakura
text: Blooms twice: a scatter in October and a fuller show in spring. The autumn flowering is sparse on purpose, not a failure.

name: kisetsu-kawazu
title: Kawazu-zakura
text: The early one. Deep pink and open in February while everything else is bare, which makes it look impatient.

name: kisetsu-fugenzo
title: Fugenzo
text: Named for two leaf-like pistils in the centre said to resemble Fugen's elephant. Double, pink, very late.

name: kisetsu-ichiyo
title: Ichiyo
text: Pale double pink with a single leaf-like pistil, hence the name. Opens after Somei-yoshino and holds longer.

name: kisetsu-omoigawa
title: Omoigawa
text: A modern selection from Tochigi, semi-double and soft pink, and one of the few named cherries younger than the cars under it.

name: kisetsu-jigokudani-troop
title: Jigokudani, the troop
text: Jigokudani Monkey Park, Nagano. The troop that learned to bathe, reportedly from one young female in the early 1960s; the behaviour spread by imitation and is now a tradition.

name: kisetsu-jigokudani-one
title: Jigokudani, one in the pool
text: One macaque, shoulders under. Steam is the only white in the frame and the face is the only loud colour.

name: kisetsu-jigokudani-snow
title: Snow on the shoulders
text: Snow settles on a wet head and does not melt, because the body below the waterline is warm and the head is not.

name: kisetsu-shimokita-limit
title: Shimokita, the northern limit
text: The Shimokita Peninsula in Aomori: the northernmost wild non-human primates on earth, a metre of snow for months, and no hot pool laid on.

name: kisetsu-mother-infant
title: Mother and infant
text: An infant rides high and dry. Grooming and bathing are both social, and the pool is a place where rank gets negotiated quietly.

name: kisetsu-noboribetsu
title: Noboribetsu, Hokkaido
text: Hokkaido steam, drawn honestly: Noboribetsu's own Jigokudani, sulphur vents and no monkeys, because macaques do not live on Hokkaido at all.

name: kisetsu-yudanaka-night
title: Yudanaka, after dark
text: The valley after the park closes. Lantern light on water, steam going straight up because there is no wind in a gorge.

name: kisetsu-thaw
title: First thaw
text: The end of the set and the end of the season: less steam, more rock, and the troop beginning to sit on the edge rather than in it.
